### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A20's outgoing transitions were spread almost evenly over A30, A31, A36, A37 and A38 (roughly 19–23% each); in the later window, about 995 in 1000 of them go to A22, with the five previous successors nearly unobserved (about 0.5%). [DIR001]
- In the earlier window, A21 was always followed by A25; in the later window that share drops to about 1 in 200 outgoing transitions, and A21 instead leads to one of A30, A31, A36, A37, A38 (about 16–23% each). [DIR002]
- In the earlier window, each of A30, A31, A36, A37 and A38 had A22 among its successors (about 18–22% of outgoing transitions, alongside the other four block members); in the later window A22 is practically no longer observed as their successor, while A25 appears at about 18–23%. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]
- The order between A21/A22 and the five activities reversed completely: earlier, each of the five ran before A21 and before A22 in 100% of traces; in the later window, A21 precedes each of the five, and A22 precedes each of the five, in about 99.5% of traces. All ten pairs still co-occur in essentially every trace in both windows. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- Relative positions shifted consistently: the five activities moved later in the trace (mean relative position from about 0.44 to about 0.60), while A22 (about 0.52 to 0.39) and A21 (about 0.65 to 0.52) moved earlier. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]
- The former adjacencies collapsed: earlier, the ordered pairs (A20, each of the five) and (each of the five, A22) occurred within five steps in all 200 traces; in the later window each of these pairs occurs within five steps in only about 1 trace, so these items' later-window profiles rest on a single observation each. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the five-activity block A30, A31, A36, A37, A38 now executes after A21 (and after A22) rather than before them: in the earlier window the flow ran from A20 into the block, the block exited to A22, and A21 followed later, always closing into A25; in the later window A20 leads directly to A22, A21 leads into the block, and the block closes into A25. This rests on the complete and uniform order reversal between A21/A22 and each of the five while co-occurrence stays at 100% (which rules out a participation change), on the rewired successors on both sides of the block, and on the consistent position shifts; 34 items qualified against roughly 0.55 expected for an unchanged process, and every item's difference exceeds about 99.5% of random re-splits. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]

Limitations: the items largely describe one underlying rearrangement rather than independent confirmations, and the evidence shows relative order only — it cannot distinguish "the block moved later" from "A21 and A22 moved earlier", nor does it cover the mutual order of A21 and A22 or what happens between them in the later window (A22 and A25 are not analysed as routing sources). The later-window LAG profiles rest on one observation each and were not relied on. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]

DIR002: source A21. Before: only A25 (1.0) — A21 always followed by A25. After: A30 (0.2), A37 (0.23), A25 (0.005), A36 (0.215), A38 (0.16), A31 (0.19) — spread across five successors (A30, A31, A36, A37, A38) with A25 nearly gone.
